reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Russell fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass: Guide Jerry Kotal (706-988-0860) reports that in October bass will normally be caught on the bottom in deep water in both the main lake and creeks. In addition to live bait they typically take drop shot rigs and jigging spoons. It’s also worth looking out for schooling action.
Crappie: Guide Wendell Wilson reports that October is often one of the very best months for Lake Russell crappie. Fish can be caught in the creeks around brush, and sometimes they will also be in open water following bait schools. Both jigs and minnows should catch fish this month

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Clarks Hill (Lake Thurmond) fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass: Guide Josh Rockefeller (706-513-6152) and tournament angler Tyler Matthews report that in October schooling action should be widespread on Thurmond, and there should also be a lot of fish moving back into the creeks. Topwater lures that imitate shad and herring will work well until it gets really cool, and then a square-bill crankbait will be hard to beat. You can usually still catch fish on a buzzbait in the first part of the month but by the end of October that can get less effective.
Crappie: Little River Guide Service reports that in October fish will likely gang up around mid-depth brush piles and submerged timber. Generally creeks in the middle and upper part of the lake…

reports.title: Lake Wylie fishing report
reports.text:
Bass bass: Tournament angler Reid McGinn of Fort Mill reports that after a long and fairly tough summer, the fall usually offers improvement in the fishing. In October schooling activity should get more widespread, and fish will be caught in both the creeks and the main lake. Topwater lures should fish well this month and there will also be fish caught on Rattle Traps. Some fish will be around the banks while others will stay offshore. And as usual on Wylie, jigs and worms should catch fish around docks.

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Greenwood fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass: Veteran tournament angler Stan Gunter of Greenwood reports that in October bass fishing should improve on Lake Greenwood, and some of the best fishing will be found in shallow water. Fish will move progressively further into the creeks where Shad Raps and lipless crankbaits will work, and by the end of the month there should be schooling activity in the backs. Of course, another group of fish will probably stay offshore where anglers will primarily target them with forward-facing sonar.

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Monticello fishing report
reports.text: Black bass: Tournament angler Eric Enlow of Union reports that in October there are usually a couple of productive patterns. Early and late you can fish shallow with topwater lures such as walking baits, and during the day you can find deeper fish that will take moving baits fished close to the bottom around structure when there is some current. In calm conditions you often need to slow down with soft plastics.

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Murray fishing report
reports.text:
Black Bass: Tournament angler Andy Wicker of Pomaria reports that it was a tough September on Murray, but at least for the first few weeks of October there is traditionally a good bite for suspended fish offshore with topwater lures and flukes. There also generally begins to be a migration of bait into the creeks, and downsized spinnerbaits and crankbaits can be effective. Finally, don’t overlook a buzzbait throughout the month.
Crappie: Captain Brad Taylor reports that typically in October fish will gang up in the creeks in large schools and gorge on threadfin shad. Some fish will usually be suspended in about the middle of the water column where you can cast or troll for them. It can also…

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Wateree fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass: Tournament angler Dearal Rodgers of Camden reports that bass fishing usually picks up this month as temperatures cool. In October bass will follow schools of shad, with some fish moving into the creeks and suspending near the bait. Shad-colored crankbaits, lipless crankbaits, and spinnerbaits will all catch fish. Also look for the topwater bite to continue to improve off points and around bait and grass.
Crappie: Veteran tournament angler Will Hinson of Cassatt reports that at some point in October fish will typically move off brush and head into the creek channels where they will suspend and chase schools of bait. They will usually get higher in the water column as it cools…

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Santee Cooper fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass: Captain David Murdaugh Sr. (843-452-9566) reports that as it gets cooler in October fish typically start to follow shad shallower. September is usually a tough month on Santee, but October can be much better. In addition to soft plastics, swimbaits and Chatterbaits may produce in shallow water. The topwater bite should also get better this month. Expect grass to continue to be a magnet for fish.
Crappie: Captain Steve English (843-729-4044) reports that by the end of September the fishing had picked up, and in October the bite should continue to improve around mid-depth brush. This September they caught decent sizes and fair numbers of fish, so there is room for optimism. Jigs…

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Jocassee fishing report
reports.text: Trout and black bass: Guide Sam Jones (864-280-9056) reports that October and November can have some of the tougher trout fishing of the year on Lake Jocassee, but after another strong summer and a decent September they expect to catch trout this month. Even though big numbers of fish are unlikely to be caught, there is still the chance to catch a trophy trout this month, and in general they should be oriented to treetops in deeper water. Trolling live bait or spoons is the preferred technique. Even on days when trout are not biting they usually pick up several bass fishing this way, and by putting out a couple of shallower lines with crankbaits the odds go up further. Most detailed Lake…

reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Keowee fishing report
reports.text: Black Bass: Guide Charles Townson (864-324-2065) reports that as water temperatures cool during October the morning bite on points and shallow humps will improve with topwater lures, swimbaits, and crankbaits. There should also continue to be schooling activity all over the lake well into the month and likely into November with things running a little behind due to the long summer. reports.source: South Carolina DNR freshwater fishing trends
reports.title: Lake Hartwell fishing report
reports.text:
Black Bass: Guide Lane Clark (864-254-8614) reports that when water temperatures drop into the lower 70s there should be widespread schooling activity across the lake, and in October fish should also be more willing to eat a variety of topwater baits as they get onto larger bait. While there will still be an offshore bite also look for more fish to move into the creeks where they can be caught on buzzbaits or jigs.
Crappie: Guide Rodney Donald (864-356-0143) reports that in October fish are usually found around brush in the creek runs, but with water levels so low he will probably be fishing deeper docks more this month. Both minnows and jigs will work.
